3: Compute the result for a game of Hex / Polygon.

5: The abstract boardgame known as [Hex][hex] / Polygon / CON-TAC-TIX is quite simple in rules, though complex in practice.
6: Two players place stones on a parallelogram with hexagonal fields.
7: The player to connect his/her stones to the opposite side first wins.
8: The four sides of the parallelogram are divided between the two players (i.e. one player gets assigned a side and the side directly opposite it and the other player gets assigned the two other sides).
9: 
10: Your goal is to build a program that given a simple representation of a board computes the winner (or lack thereof).
11: Note that all games need not be "fair".
12: (For example, players may have mismatched piece counts or the game's board might have a different width and height.)
13:

17: . O . X .
18:  . X X O .
19:   O O O X .
20:    . X O X O
21:     X O O O X
22: ```
23: 
24: "Player `O`" plays from top to bottom, "Player `X`" plays from left to right.
25: In the above example `O` has made a connection from left to right but nobody has won since `O` didn't connect top and bottom.

func neighbors(r, c, rows, cols int) [][2]int {
	n := [][2]int{
		{r, c - 1}, {r, c + 1},
		{r - 1, c}, {r - 1, c + 1},
		{r + 1, c}, {r + 1, c - 1},
	}
	var out [][2]int
	for _, p := range n {
		if p[0] >= 0 && p[0] < rows && p[1] >= 0 && p[1] < cols {
			out = append(out, p)

	}
	return out

func connects(board [][]rune, player rune, rows, cols int, isStart, isGoal func(r, c int) bool) bool {
	visited := make([][]bool, rows)
	for i := range visited {
		visited[i] = make([]bool, cols)
	}
	queue := [][2]int{}
	for r := 0; r < rows; r++ {
		for c := 0; c < cols; c++ {
			if board[r][c] == player && isStart(r, c) {
				queue = append(queue, [2]int{r, c})
				visited[r][c] = true
			}
		}
	}
	for len(queue) > 0 {
		cur := queue[0]
		queue = queue[1:]
		r, c := cur[0], cur[1]
		if isGoal(r, c) {
			return true

		for _, p := range neighbors(r, c, rows, cols) {
			nr, nc := p[0], p[1]
			if !visited[nr][nc] && board[nr][nc] == player {
				visited[nr][nc] = true
				queue = append(queue, [2]int{nr, nc})
			}

	}

package connect

// ResultOf reports the winner of a game of Hex / Polygon.
//
// Player "O" connects the top edge to the bottom edge, while player
// "X" connects the left edge to the right edge. The first player to form
// such a connection wins. If no player has a connection the result is "".
func ResultOf(lines []string) (string, error) {
	if len(lines) == 0 {
		return "", nil
	}

	rows := len(lines)
	cols := len(lines[0])
	if cols == 0 {
		return "", nil
	}

	// O plays from top to bottom.
	if connects(lines, 'O', rows, cols,
		func(r, c int) bool { return r == 0 },
		func(r, c int) bool { return r == rows-1 },
	) {
		return "O", nil
	}

	// X plays from left to right.
	if connects(lines, 'X', rows, cols,
		func(r, c int) bool { return c == 0 },
		func(r, c int) bool { return c == cols-1 },
	) {
		return "X", nil
	}

	return "", nil
}
```
